To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the control energy of a complex network is a function of the number of control and network nodes, and of the network weights and topology.

(i) the number of control inputs needed to symmetrically control a complex network depends on the network topology; (ii) the controllability of a network can be characterized in terms of its spectral properties; (iii) the control energy depends both on the network topology (through the number of control units) and on the network weights (through the controllability metrics).

(i) the controllability energy increases exponentially with network size, if the number and location of the control nodes are constant; (ii) the controllabilty energy depends on network topology and weights, and on the number of control clusters; (iii) we propose a distributed control strategy with controllability guarantees for complex networks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the controllability of complex networks
the controllability of complex networks and it is motivated by applications in which the control energy is a critical performance metric.
the fundamental question of how to control complex networks with a limited number of control nodes and with limited control energy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in general, complex networks are controllable with small energy and small number of nodes.
the number of control inputs is the main factor that affects the controllability of a complex network.
the controllability of a complex network is determined by its topology, weights and dimension.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, while the controllability of complex networks is limited, there are strategies that can effectively control them.
the number of nodes and their coupling strength limit the controllability of complex networks, and that distributed control strategies can effectively overcome such limitations.
, while it is possible to control complex networks, the energy needed for control increases with network dimension.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, while complex network controllability is in general difficult, we can design control strategies with performance guarantees and limited energy consumption, if we exploit the network partitioning structure.
, despite the classic notion, few nodes are not in practice able to control symmetric complex networks.

, while the control energy of complex networks is in general exponential in the network dimension, we can design distributed control strategies with performance guarantees, and with energy that is only dependent on the controllibility of the clusters.
